title: Fun Facts
text:
10 Fun Facts About Meerkats

Meerkats live in groups called mobs.

A mob can have up to around 30 meerkats, and they work together to survive.

They take turns being the lookout.

While the rest of the mob searches for food, one meerkat often stands upright and watches for predators.

Meerkats are immune to some venom.

They have some resistance to the venom of scorpions and certain snakes, which helps them hunt these dangerous animals.

They can close their ears when digging.

Special flaps of skin cover their ear openings, keeping dirt out while they’re digging.

Meerkats have dark patches around their eyes.

These help reduce glare from the intense African sun.

They live in underground burrows.

Meerkats dig extensive tunnel systems where they sleep, raise their young, and escape extreme heat and predators.

They’re surprisingly fast diggers.

Meerkats can move enormous amounts of dirt using their powerful front claws.

Baby meerkats are raised by the whole mob.

Older siblings and other adults help babysit, protect, and feed the pups.

They have different calls for different dangers.

Meerkats use a variety of vocalizations to communicate, including different alarm calls depending on the type of predator.

They spend a lot of time standing on two legs.

Their famous upright pose isn’t just for looking cute—they’re often scanning the surrounding area for danger.

title: Find A Meerkat Near You
text:
Rosamond Gifford Zoo — Syracuse, NY

About 1 hour 15 minutes from Ithaca
Exhibit: Social Animals Building
Address: 1 Conservation Place, Syracuse, NY 13204
The zoo currently lists slender-tailed meerkats as one of its animals.

Buffalo Zoo — Buffalo, NY

About 2 hours 30 minutes from Ithaca
Exhibit: Gorilla House
Address: 300 Parkside Avenue, Buffalo, NY 14214
The meerkat exhibit is located inside the Gorilla House and is open year-round.

Pittsburgh Zoo & Aquarium — Pittsburgh, PA

About 3 hours 30 minutes from Ithaca
Exhibit: Worlds of Discovery
Address: 7370 Baker Street, Pittsburgh, PA 15206
The zoo currently lists meerkats in its animal collection and places them in Worlds of Discovery.

Philadelphia Zoo — Philadelphia, PA

About 4 hours from Ithaca
Exhibit: Meerkat Maze
Address: 3400 W. Girard Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19104
The zoo has a dedicated Meerkat Maze, where visitors can watch the meerkats explore, dig, and climb.

Cleveland Metroparks Zoo — Cleveland, OH

About 4 hours 15 minutes from Ithaca
Exhibit: African Elephant Crossing / African Savanna
Address: 3900 Wildlife Way, Cleveland, OH 44109
The zoo’s animal resources currently list the slender-tailed meerkat, although some of its online animal resources note that listings can include historical information.
